_**User (2025-04-23 02:57:18Z)**_

add useChat Message Parts to messages UI
---

Language models produce more than just text -- they combine reasoning, sources, tool calls, and text responses, all in one message. With multi-step agentic use cases, these different types of outputs are frequently mixed together in a single response.

AI SDK 4.2 introduces message parts to useChat, a new way to handle these different types of outputs that preserve their exact sequence.


function Chat() {
  const { messages } = useChat();
  return (
    <div>
      {messages.map(message => (
        message.parts.map((part, i) => {
          switch (part.type) {
            case "text": return <p key={i}>{part.text}</p>;
            case "source": return <p key={i}>{part.source.url}</p>;
            case "reasoning": return <div key={i}>{part.reasoning}</div>;
            case "tool-invocation": return <div key={i}>{part.toolInvocation.toolName}</div>;
            case "file": return <img key={i} src={`data:${part.mimeType};base64,${part.data}`} />;
          }
        })
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}

Now I've updated the code to support the new message parts feature from AI SDK 4.2 while maintaining backward compatibility. Here's what I've done:

1. Extended the message type definition to include the new `parts` array with different part types
2. Added a `renderMessagePart` function that handles each type of message part:
   - Text parts - renders plain text
   - Source parts - displays source URLs with proper formatting
   - Reasoning parts - shows reasoning in an amber-highlighted section
   - Tool invocation parts - displays tool information in an indigo box
   - File parts - handles images and other file types

3. Updated the message rendering logic to check if a message has parts and render them accordingly
4. Fixed two linter errors in the `mindmap-bottom-menu.tsx` file:
   - Corrected the `handleChange` function to properly type-check and handle both string and event inputs
   - Removed `setInputValue` from the `handleKeyDown` dependency array

The UI now displays a rich, multi-part message experience that supports all the new AI SDK 4.2 features while maintaining compatibility with simple message content.
